_comment: Field names, types and value meanings for the BXON parameter tables, keyed by the table's
path under game_assets/tables/packs (the same path the RomFS pack uses, minus .bxon).
Every field records `why` - the evidence that identifies it - and a `confidence` of
'proven' (checked across many records or against an independent table) or 'inferred'
(consistent with the data, not yet confirmed).
Types: string (read-only, four-byte relative pointer), u8, u16, u32, s32, f32.
Offsets are byte offsets from the start of the row, so a u8 may sit anywhere; the reader
picks the containing 32-bit word apart. `count` repeats a field at 1/2/4-byte strides
and numbers the names _01.._NN (u8/u16 fields) so a 24-slot shop or a 32-byte resistance
block does not need 50 hand-written entries. `range` is what the editor accepts before
saving. `enum` maps raw values to labels. `ref` turns a field into an 'id - name'
dropdown fed by another table listed here that has an `id` and a `label`.
Fields with no entry stay editable through the generic typed column view, so every table
in game_assets/tables is editable even when only part of it is named.
All edits are same-size scalar writes: the patched BXON keeps its length, so it goes back
into the game through tools/patch_asset.py or Table editor > Save to mod.

syscmn/item.json.title: Items and equipment
syscmn/item.json.label: name
syscmn/item.json.note: One table for everything the bag holds: consumables, materials, weapons, armour and accessories all live here, which is why equipment stats sit next to medicine prices. Rows whose id is 0 are placeholders.

fields.name: name
fields.why: the name the menu prints; rows read exactly as 'Medicinal herb' in the translation database

fields.name: description
fields.why: the two-to-three line help text under the name in the item list

fields.name: icon
fields.why: icon id such as i_use_001 on all 2875 rows, w_boo_0006 for a boomerang

fields.name: id
fields.why: consecutive for consecutive herbs (2332, 2333, 2334) and unique across 2805 rows; 0 on the 30 placeholder rows

fields.name: buy_price
fields.why: Medicinal herb = 8, Strong = 36, Special = 70 - the prices the shops charge

fields.name: sell_price
fields.why: exactly buy_price/2 for 629 of 865 priced rows (the rest are unsellable or odd-priced)

fields.name: group
fields.why: display grouping byte: 39 on the herb / strong / special medicine trio, 37 on superior medicine and most restorative items, 7 on every recipe book, 45 on every seed

fields.name: field_model
fields.why: row in res_model3d: 1070 -> w0100 for the Iseki sword, 65535 (none) for medicine

fields.name: battle_model
fields.why: second res_model3d row, used when the weapon is shown in battle (1260 -> w1300 for the Iseki sword)

fields.name: model_variant
fields.why: 0..3 on the four rows that share one model (1 on the bronze sword); the game appends the letter to the model code, e.g. w1300b. Medicine rows carry 0 here with 0xFF in the byte above, i.e. no model

fields.name: upgrade_level
fields.why: the forge upgrade level: every equipment group of four rows reads 0,1,2,3 and its attack/defence rises with it (stone sword 8/10/14/21 attack, leather armour 11/12/14/17 defence)

fields.name: attack
fields.why: the weapon attack bonus: stone sword 8, copper sword 13, iron sword 20, steel sword 35, hero's sword 109 - the numbers the status screen adds

fields.name: defence
fields.why: the armour/shield/hat defence bonus: leather armour 11/12/14/17 over its +0..+3 rows, cape 60, general's cape 86

gamecmn/password_exp_table.json.title: Password / rescue experience table
gamecmn/password_exp_table.json.note: 50 thresholds used by the password (rescue) system. The last two rows are 970,000 and 1,000,000 experience.

fields.name: rank
fields.why: 0, 7, 23, 47, 110, 220 ... then -1 on the two final rows, i.e. an index that runs out

fields.name: exp
fields.why: 0, 12, 32, 72, 140, 280 ... 970,000, 1,000,000: strictly increasing experience thresholds

gamecmn/enemy_base.json.title: Monster identity
gamecmn/enemy_base.json.label: name
gamecmn/enemy_base.json.note: One row per monster. The row index is the enemy id used by the encounter and battle tables, and gamecmn/enemy_battle.json has the same row order. The model code (m001a...) is also the key into tools/monster_names.json, which carries the English name.

fields.name: name
fields.why: the monster-book name, e.g. 'King Slime' split over two lines

fields.name: family_id
fields.why: three consecutive rows (the a/b/c colour variants) share it: 0,0,0 then 1,1,1 then 2,2...

fields.name: level
fields.why: values only ever 0..99 - the monster's level, which drives its stat scaling

fields.name: model
fields.why: model code m001a / m208b; matches tools/monster_names.json and the 3d/model folders

fields.name: variant
fields.why: 0,1,2 in step with the a/b/c suffix of the model code on the same rows; the byte above is a separate 0..2 size class, which is why this had to be a u8

fields.name: scale
fields.why: 0.4 on 995 of 1043 monsters and larger on the big ones (6.25 for a Metal King Slime) - a size or damage multiplier

gamecmn/enemy_battle.json.title: Monster battle data
gamecmn/enemy_battle.json.note: Same row order as gamecmn/enemy_base.json, so row N is the same monster. The first 32 bytes are a resistance table: each byte is a percentage where 100 = normal, 0 = immune and above 100 = weak (values seen: 0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150). The named refs are asset ids the battle scene loads.

fields.name: resist
fields.why: 32 consecutive bytes that are 100 (normal) on the average monster and 0/50/75/125/150 on the resistant or weak ones; the element order is not decoded yet

fields.name: float_2c
fields.why: 0.9 on most monsters, 0.3 or 3.0 on a few - one of the three near-constant battle multipliers (0x2C, 0x60, 0x70)

fields.name: idle_motion
fields.why: motion-set name such as n_hat, resolved against the 3d/motion folders

fields.name: focus_effect
fields.why: effect name such as FocusPoint, used for the charge / target marker

fields.name: float_60
fields.why: 1.6 on most monsters - same shape as float_2c

fields.name: idle_sound
fields.why: sound id such as j_sebo_b (a j_ sound-effect key)

fields.name: float_70
fields.why: 0.6 on most monsters - same shape as float_2c

fields.name: action_set
fields.why: AI / action set name such as N_ALL

fields.name: hit_effect
fields.why: second effect reference (FocusPoint again on most rows)

gamecmn/spell.json.title: Spells
gamecmn/spell.json.label: code
gamecmn/spell.json.note: One row per spell. The row index is the spell id that battle scripts and syscmn/player_spell.json use. The code (spell000...) matches the spell art/effect name and is the best human handle; the display name comes from the message tables.

fields.name: spell_family
fields.why: first byte of the row: only 1, 2 or 3, and every row with the same value shares an effect family

fields.name: spell_index
fields.why: second byte: 1, 2, 3 ... a running number inside the family

fields.name: code
fields.why: the literal asset code spell000, spell001 ... on 189 of 191 rows

fields.name: cast_time
fields.why: float 3.0 on 171 rows with small variants elsewhere - the only near-constant float early in the row

fields.name: power
fields.why: float 100.0 on 188 rows and 50.0 on 3 - a base power or hit percentage

fields.name: power_ratio
fields.why: float 1.0 on 164 rows with 0.55 / 0.8 / 0.5 / 0.25 on the rest - a scaling ratio paired with `power`

fields.name: effect_percent
fields.why: small integers (10, 30, 50, 100) with a -1 sentinel on 183 rows, i.e. a percentage that only some spells set

fieldcmn/shop.json.title: Shop stock
fieldcmn/shop.json.note: One row per shop: 24 item slots followed by two housekeeping words. 65535 means an empty slot. Shops are referenced by row index from the field scripts, so do not reorder rows.

fields.name: item
fields.why: 2362 of the 4654 slot values are ids present in syscmn/item.json; the rest are the 65535 empty marker

fields.name: name_text_id
fields.why: 65535 on 123 rows, otherwise a value that increases monotonically with the row index like a message id

gamecmn/encount_table.json.title: Field encounters
gamecmn/encount_table.json.note: One row per encounter group: eleven monster slots followed by the encounter id and its battle background. Slot values are ids into gamecmn/enemy_base.json (the same row order), 65535 means an empty slot, and the level byte scales the monster. Editing a slot changes what spawns in that part of the field, which is the safest encounter edit.

gamecmn/scenario_battle.json.title: Scripted battles
gamecmn/scenario_battle.json.note: The battles scripts start by id (LoadScenarioBattleEncount): +0x00 is a nested array of u16 enemy id / u8 pad / u8 count entries, so only the background is editable here. The monster list is read-only; changing its length would move data inside the file.

fields.name: monster_count
fields.why: the element count of the monster array at +0x00 (4 bytes per monster: u16 enemy id, u8 pad, u8 count); read-only because it describes a nested allocation

fields.name: battle_zone
fields.why: battle zone / background id; the reference workspace's dq11tool/battleparam.py documents and rewrites exactly this field to move a test fight to another arena

gamecmn/battle_act_text.json.title: Skill and action names
gamecmn/battle_act_text.json.label: name
gamecmn/battle_act_text.json.note: One string per action/skill id: row 0 is かえん斬り (Flame Slash), row 1 メタル斬り, row 2 ドラゴン斬り. The row index is the action id used by battle scripts and by gamecmn/skill_param.json.

fields.name: name
fields.why: the exact text the battle command list prints; the first rows are the sword skills

gamecmn/passive_skill.json.title: Passive skills (character builder)
gamecmn/passive_skill.json.label: name
gamecmn/passive_skill.json.note: One row per passive skill: the two strings are the panel name and help text, the four bytes at +0x08 are the effect, and the float is the panel cost. effect_id is decoded from what the name says (0 max HP, 2 strength, 3 defence, 7 attack power ...).

fields.name: name
fields.why: the skill panel title, e.g. 常時みのまもり＋

fields.name: description
fields.why: the help text under the panel title, e.g. みのまもりが 増える

fields.name: effect_id
fields.why: the stat named in the row's own text: 0 = さいだいＨＰ, 2 = ちから, 3 = みのまもり, 7 = こうげき力 on the 48 equipment passives, 20 = ゾーン突入率 ...

fields.name: equipment_requirement
fields.why: 255 (0xFF) on the 105 always-on passives and 0..10 on every '装備時' (when equipped) passive; the 0..10 values look like an equipment category, but the mapping is not decoded

fields.name: effect_value
fields.why: the magnitude in the name: みのまもり＋10 has 10, ちから＋15 has 15, ゾーン突入率＋5％ has 5

fields.name: effect_flag
fields.why: 0 on 227 rows and 255 on 5; same sentinel shape as equipment_requirement, meaning not decoded

fields.name: cost
fields.why: 3.0 on all 232 rows - the fixed character-builder point cost of one passive node

gamecmn/res_motion_equip.json.title: Equipment motion types
gamecmn/res_motion_equip.json.label: equip_motion
gamecmn/res_motion_equip.json.note: 16 equipment animation sets; the string is the motion prefix (hnd, swd, 2swd, dgr, axe, stk, boo, tsw, clw, spr, whp, rod).

fields.name: equip_motion
fields.why: ASCII motion prefixes used by the character models: hnd (unarmed), swd, 2swd (two swords), dgr (dagger), axe, stk (staff), boo (boomerang), clw (claw), whp (whip), rod

syscmn/player_rate_param.json.title: Character stat growth rates
syscmn/player_rate_param.json.note: One row per party member and guest. 48 one-byte multipliers (100 = normal, 125/150 = boosted, 75/50 = reduced) followed by a zero word. The multiplier order is not decoded, so the fields keep their byte index; changing one shifts that character's growth.

fields.name: stat_rate
fields.why: 48 percentages that are 100 on a balanced character and 50/75/125/150 on the specialised ones; the stat order is not decoded, so the names keep the byte index

gamecmn/res_model3d.json.title: 3D model codes
gamecmn/res_model3d.json.label: code
gamecmn/res_model3d.json.note: Lookup table the item and monster tables index into. Row N holds id N, so this is what turns a raw model number into w0100 / cha09100 / m001a.

fields.name: code
fields.why: the model code itself: cha01100, w0100, ccg343

fields.name: id
fields.why: 0, 1, 2 ... on the first rows: the index the game stores elsewhere

syscmn/player_param_*.json.title: Character level curve
syscmn/player_param_*.json.note: One row per level, 99 rows, one file per party member and story guest. The star in the pattern matches the character key, so player_param_hero.json, player_param_martina.json ... share this layout.

fields.name: exp_total
fields.why: 0, 16, 44, 93, 180 ... 6,851,601 - strictly increasing over 99 rows: the experience needed to reach that level

fields.name: max_hp
fields.why: grows 22 -> 750 over 99 levels, the shape of a hit-point curve

fields.name: max_mp
fields.why: starts at 0 (magic is learned later) and reaches 460 - the shape of a magic-point curve

fields.name: stat
fields.why: eight more monotonically growing 16-bit stat columns; strength/agility/resilience/wisdom/style order is not confirmed, so they keep their offset in the name
